categories.name: Kitchen Appliance
categories.description: Mixers, kettles, toasters, blenders, and countertop cooking appliances

safetyFlags.label: Burning smell or melting plastic odor
Exposed mains wiring or frayed power cord
Liquid entered motor or electronics enclosure

repurposeIdeas.title: Stainless Steel Herb Planter
repurposeIdeas.description: Transform durable stainless kettle or blender carafe into a rustic kitchen planter.

repurposeIdeas.title: Workshop Hardware Organizer
repurposeIdeas.description: Use glass or heavy plastic canisters to sort nails, bolts, and small workshop items.

repurposeIdeas.title: Industrial Accent Lamp
repurposeIdeas.description: Repurpose the vintage metallic appliance chassis into a striking bedside lamp housing.

reuseRoutes: Donate to community soup kitchen or student flat if non-critical features still function
Pass along to an appliance repair trainee for bench practice
Offer as 'for parts / spares' on local marketplace or Freecycle

repair: Unplug from 230V mains socket and let heating elements cool completely.
Inspect cord and plug pins for scorch marks or copper wire fatigue.
Remove bottom base plate with insulated screwdriver to examine switches and thermal fuse.
Test continuity across heating coils using a digital multimeter before reassembly.
reuse: Wipe exterior with food-safe vinegar solution and clear crumbs or scale.
Tag with clear label noting any minor cosmetic or switch quirks.
Bundle with original lid, attachments, and power lead.
repurpose: Completely remove motor core and internal electrical harnesses.
File down sharp metal edges and seal screw holes with silicone.
Drill base drainage holes if repurposing into a garden pot.
replace: Look for BEE 5-star energy rated models with minimum 2-year warranty.
Check manufacturer commitment to 5-year spare parts availability.
Avail old appliance exchange discount to ensure responsible retailer pickup.
recycle: Do not dispose in municipal wet/dry garbage bin.
Separate detachable glass carafes and stainless vessels for scrap metal collection.
Drop off electrical motor base at authorized e-waste collection kiosk.

commonFaults.label: Stripped Drive Coupler Teeth
commonFaults.name: Stripped Drive Coupler Teeth
commonFaults.description: Rubber or nylon drive teeth rounded off from ice overload, causing motor to spin freely.
diySteps: Unplug appliance completely.
Hold motor shaft underneath with flathead screwdriver or cloth.
Unscrew coupler clockwise (reverse thread) and replace with identical replacement coupler.
Tighten securely and test with empty jar.

commonFaults.label: Auto-Shutoff Bimetal Switch Stuck
commonFaults.name: Auto-Shutoff Bimetal Switch Stuck
commonFaults.description: Steam bimetal strip fails to trigger switch off automatically when boiling.
diySteps: Unplug base and open kettle handle access screws.
Inspect steam tube channel for lime-scale deposits blocking vapor flow.
Gently clean contacts with isopropyl alcohol or replace standard T125 thermostat switch.
Reassemble handle and boil clean water to verify auto cut-off.

commonFaults.label: Worn Motor Carbon Brushes
commonFaults.name: Worn Motor Carbon Brushes
commonFaults.description: Motor sparks intermittently and runs sluggishly due to carbon brushes worn past minimum length.
diySteps: Unscrew motor base enclosure.
Unclip brass brush retainer springs.
Slide out worn carbon blocks and measure commutator ring surface.
Insert fresh brush pair and clip retainers back.

commonFaults.label: Blown Heating Element / Coil
commonFaults.name: Blown Heating Element / Coil
commonFaults.description: Appliance powers on indicator light but base produces zero heat.
diySteps: Check continuity across element terminals using multimeter resistance mode.
Detach heat-resistant push terminals and remove mounting flange nuts.
Fit matching OEM replacement heating ring or cartridge with new heatproof silicone gasket.

commonFaults.label: Acrid Burning Odor / Coil Insulation Melting
commonFaults.name: Acrid Burning Odor / Coil Insulation Melting
commonFaults.description: Burnt varnish or melted wire sheath causing intense smoking and severe short circuit hazard.
diySteps: DO NOT USE DIY FIX. Requires professional coil rewinding or high-voltage insulation bench testing.

commonFaults.label: Exposed Mains Copper Wire / Frayed Cable
commonFaults.name: Exposed Mains Copper Wire / Frayed Cable
commonFaults.description: Outer PVC jacket torn at strain-relief boot, revealing live mains conductors.
diySteps: Unplug immediately. Do not attempt tape-only repairs on 16A mains.
Open bottom cord clamp, trim off fatigued cable section.
Strip fresh insulation, crimp spade connectors, and anchor firmly into strain relief boot.

categories.name: Phone or Laptop
categories.description: Smartphones, notebooks, ultrabooks, and touch tablets

safetyFlags.label: Swollen puffy lithium pouch or pushed-out screen
Hot thermal scorch smell or smoking port

repurposeIdeas.title: Dedicated HD Wireless Security Cam
repurposeIdeas.description: Install IP Webcam software to turn old phone into an always-on pet or front door camera.

repurposeIdeas.title: Wall-Mounted Smart Home Dashboard
repurposeIdeas.description: Mount tablet to wall running Home Assistant, Spotify controller, or digital calendar.

repurposeIdeas.title: Low-Power Linux Home Server
repurposeIdeas.description: Install Ubuntu Server on old laptop to host local backups, Pi-hole DNS, or media vault.

reuseRoutes: Wipe clean and pass to student or elderly relative for video calls and web browsing
Trade in via official manufacturer or Cashify exchange for cash credit
Keep as emergency dual-SIM backup device in car or desk drawer

repair: Back up all local documents and personal photos to cloud or USB.
Perform full system shutdown and disconnect charger.
Use ESD anti-static wrist strap and plastic spudgers when prying casing.
Test touch digitizer, microphones, and camera before sealing adhesive.
reuse: Log out of Google/Apple ID accounts and perform full factory reset.
Clean chassis with 70% isopropyl wipes.
Apply fresh tempered glass screen guard to protect display.
repurpose: Enable developer options and USB debugging if deploying as server.
Configure battery charge limiter to 60-80% to protect battery under 24/7 power.
Uninstall bloatware apps to maximize CPU performance.
replace: Check manufacturer OS software update support window (prefer 5+ years).
Select model with modular user-replaceable battery if possible.
Opt for standard USB-PD charging port compliance.
recycle: Cryptographically wipe internal NAND flash or remove SSD storage drive.
Never discard lithium battery into municipal trash bins.
Drop at authorized R2 or e-Stewards certified electronics recycler.

commonFaults.label: Swollen Puffy Lithium Battery (Display Lifting)
commonFaults.name: Swollen Puffy Lithium Battery (Display Lifting)
commonFaults.description: Gas buildup in lithium pouch causing acute fire/thermal runaway hazard.
diySteps: CRITICAL SAFETY HAZARD. Immediately stop charging and power off device.
Do not puncture, squeeze, or apply heat to the battery pouch.
Take immediately to certified technician equipped with fire-safe sand buckets.

commonFaults.label: Degraded Battery (Shuts down below 30%)
commonFaults.name: Degraded Battery (Shuts down below 30%)
commonFaults.description: Chemical capacity decayed under 75% health after years of charging cycles.
diySteps: Heat rear perimeter with warm gel pack to soften adhesive gasket.
Use suction cup and plastic guitar pick to gently lift back cover.
Unscrew battery bracket, disconnect flex cable, pull release adhesive tabs.
Install fresh OEM battery cell and reapply adhesive perimeter.

commonFaults.label: Cracked Front Glass / Touch Display
commonFaults.name: Cracked Front Glass / Touch Display
commonFaults.description: Spiderweb glass fracture from drop impact; touch digitizer or AMOLED panel damaged.
diySteps: Apply clear packing tape over splintered glass to avoid finger cuts.
Disconnect battery connector first before disconnecting display ribbon.
Transfer ambient light sensor and speaker mesh to new display assembly.
Connect new display, test all touch points and brightness before final adhesive clamping.

commonFaults.label: Loose / Lint-Clogged USB-C Port
commonFaults.name: Loose / Lint-Clogged USB-C Port
commonFaults.description: Cable falls out easily and fast charging drops due to packed pocket lint in port recess.
diySteps: Turn off device and illuminate port with bright flashlight.
Use non-conductive wooden toothpick or plastic probe to gently extract compressed lint.
Blow dry compressed air burst to clear dislodged fibers.
Insert cable firmly until tactile click confirms full engagement.

commonFaults.label: Dust-Choked Fan / Thermal Throttling
commonFaults.name: Dust-Choked Fan / Thermal Throttling
commonFaults.description: Laptop runs burning hot and fan buzzes loudly due to dust pelt blocking heatsink fins.
diySteps: Remove bottom chassis screws and pry cover.
Hold fan blades stationary with finger so bearings do not overspin.
Brush dust felt from copper heatsink fins and vacuum gently.
Apply drop of fresh thermal paste on CPU/GPU if heat pipe was removed.

commonFaults.label: Sticky / Non-Registering Keyboard Keys
commonFaults.name: Sticky / Non-Registering Keyboard Keys
commonFaults.description: Beverage spill residue or debris underneath scissor switch hinge.
diySteps: Gently pop off offending keycap using thin pry tool.
Clean scissor mechanism and rubber dome with 99% isopropyl alcohol swab.
Allow 15 minutes to dry fully, snap keycap back down until it clicks.

categories.name: Charger or Cable
categories.description: USB power bricks, charging adapters, braided cables, and power strips

safetyFlags.label: Mains wire sheathing split or frayed
Adapter casing hot with scorched plastic smell

repurposeIdeas.title: Heavy-Duty Garden & Tool Bundlers
repurposeIdeas.description: Strip outer jacketing to make weather-resistant, flexible ties for garden vines and garage hoses.

repurposeIdeas.title: Braided Paracord-Style Keychains
repurposeIdeas.description: Weave colorful nylon braided cable outer sheath into rugged luggage tags and key lanyards.

repurposeIdeas.title: Safe 5V DIY Electronics Bench Supply
repurposeIdeas.description: Terminate cut USB cable with alligator clips for powering low-voltage hobby breadboards.

reuseRoutes: Keep as low-power bedside trickle charger for e-readers or earbuds
Leave as dedicated backup cable in office or car glove box
Donate working spare adapters to school computer clubs

repair: Verify adapter is completely disconnected from wall outlet.
Check cable continuity pin-to-pin before applying heat shrink tubing.
Slide dual-wall adhesive-lined heat shrink tubing over the cracked neck joint.
Use heat gun at 120°C to activate internal waterproof glue seal.
reuse: Clean grime with alcohol pad.
Coil in loose loop without sharp kinks.
Test on low-draw peripheral before primary device.
repurpose: Snip off broken connector ends flush.
Strip and tin red (5V) and black (GND) lead wires.
Insulate unused data lines.
replace: Choose USB-IF certified GaN chargers with over-voltage and thermal surge protection.
Prefer thick braided silicone cables rated for 100W+ USB-PD.
Verify CE / BIS safety certification stamps.
recycle: Snip off copper cords and bundle with scrap copper wire.
Drop plastic brick into municipal electronic accessory drop box.

commonFaults.label: Outer Sheath Frayed at Connector Boot
commonFaults.name: Outer Sheath Frayed at Connector Boot
commonFaults.description: Strain relief collar split open; braided shielding or internal conductors visible.
diySteps: Check internal copper strands are still intact without shorting.
Slide marine-grade adhesive-lined polyolefin heat-shrink tubing over connector head.
Shrink with heat gun or hair dryer until adhesive oozes slightly, forming stiff reinforced boot.
Add silicone cable spring collar for extra flex resistance.

commonFaults.label: Intermittent Charging (Wire Broken Inside Neck)
commonFaults.name: Intermittent Charging (Wire Broken Inside Neck)
commonFaults.description: Charges only when bent at a specific angle due to fatigue fracture in copper hair wires.
diySteps: Cut cable 2 cm back from damaged molded plug.
Strip outer jacket to expose internal conductor cores.
Solder leads onto a DIY solderable metal USB-C / Lightning plug replacement head.
Snap outer metal shielding shell and crimp strain relief.

commonFaults.label: Bent Connector Plug / Housing
commonFaults.name: Bent Connector Plug / Housing
commonFaults.description: Metal shell squished or bent from being stepped on, preventing port insertion.
diySteps: Carefully inspect interior tongue with magnifying loupe.
Use flat precision watchmaker screwdriver to gently reform outer rectangular metal shield.
Verify pins are not shorted before plugging into low-value device.

commonFaults.label: Tarnished / Blackened Gold Pins
commonFaults.name: Tarnished / Blackened Gold Pins
commonFaults.description: Blackened oxide coating on power pins causing slow or failed charging handshake.
diySteps: Dip stiff bristle interdental brush into 99% isopropyl alcohol.
Scrub contact pins back and forth vigorously to remove carbonization.
Dry with microfiber cloth and apply thin coat of DeoxIT contact cleaner.

commonFaults.label: Wall Adapter Burning Smell / Melting Shell
commonFaults.name: Wall Adapter Burning Smell / Melting Shell
commonFaults.description: Blown primary switching MOSFET or shorted transformer winding generating smoke.
diySteps: CRITICAL FIRE HAZARD. Immediately unplug from mains.
Ultrasonically welded power bricks cannot be safely opened or resealed at home.
Recycle immediately and replace with compliant charger.

categories.name: Audio Device
categories.description: Over-ear headphones, Bluetooth earbuds, desktop monitors, and portable speakers

safetyFlags.label: Swollen earbud case or bulging speaker enclosure
Burnt voice coil odor or hot amplifier circuit

repurposeIdeas.title: High-Quality Auxiliary Lapel / Desk Mic
repurposeIdeas.description: Salvage working microphone capsules and pre-amp wiring for amateur podcasting or intercoms.

repurposeIdeas.title: Retro Bluetooth Speaker Enclosure
repurposeIdeas.description: Fit a $5 Bluetooth amplifier chip inside a vintage wooden speaker cabinet with new drivers.

repurposeIdeas.title: Vibration Isolation Pads
repurposeIdeas.description: Repurpose acoustic memory foam pads to isolate turntables, 3D printers, or microphone stands.

reuseRoutes: Dedicate as stationary desktop headphones with a low-cost $2 3.5mm cable
Pass to children for online homework or audiobooks
Donate to local audio engineering classroom for component teardown study

repair: Test speaker coil impedance with multimeter (typical 32 ohms for headphones, 4-8 ohms for speakers).
Discharge any capacitors if opening powered desktop monitors.
Use flexible enameled wire solder flux when re-attaching thin audio driver voice coils.
Ensure airtight seal around speaker chamber when resealing acoustic baffle.
reuse: Sanitize ear cushions with alcohol-free disinfectant.
Store in protective zippered hard case.
Calibrate EQ via system equalizer to compensate for any slight frequency shift.
repurpose: Carefully unsolder dynamic driver capsules.
Wire drivers in parallel or series according to amplifier impedance specs.
replace: Check availability of third-party snap-on ear pad replacements.
Choose models with detachable 3.5mm or USB-C cables.
Prioritize IPX4+ water resistance for workout headphones.
recycle: Remove tiny lithium button cells from earbuds prior to recycling.
Deliver speaker drivers to scrap magnet / metal recycler.

commonFaults.label: Flaking Leatherette Ear Cushions
commonFaults.name: Flaking Leatherette Ear Cushions
commonFaults.description: Polyurethane leather flakes off in black specks onto ears, though audio drivers remain pristine.
diySteps: Gently rotate or unclip old cushion plastic retaining rings.
Clean old adhesive residue with isopropyl swab.
Stretch replacement breathable velour or cooling gel ear pads over headphone rim and click firmly into place.

commonFaults.label: Snapped Plastic Headband Arch
commonFaults.name: Snapped Plastic Headband Arch
commonFaults.description: Tension arch cracked at stress point, preventing headphones from clamping to head.
diySteps: Rough up plastic edges with 220-grit sandpaper.
Splint crack with thin flexible spring steel strip or zip-tie reinforcement.
Bond with two-part epoxy or wrap tightly with self-amalgamating silicone tape.

commonFaults.label: One Channel Silent (Frayed Jack Wire)
commonFaults.name: One Channel Silent (Frayed Jack Wire)
commonFaults.description: Sound cuts out in left or right ear unless 3.5mm plug is wiggled.
diySteps: Snip off factory molded 3.5mm plug 3 cm from bend.
Burn enamel insulation off copper hairs with lighter flame, then tin with solder flux.
Solder Left (tip), Right (ring), and Ground (sleeve) onto metal replacement 3.5mm TRS jack.

commonFaults.label: Battery Lasts Under 30 Minutes
commonFaults.name: Battery Lasts Under 30 Minutes
commonFaults.description: Internal 3.7V lithium pouch holds fraction of original charge.
diySteps: Unclip ear cup cover and unscrew internal acoustic baffle.
De-solder red (+) and black (-) leads from old lithium cell.
Fit identical dimension 3.7V lipo cell with protection circuit board.
Re-solder leads, secure with double-sided foam tape, and reassemble.

commonFaults.label: Bulging Charging Case / Swollen Lithium Cell
commonFaults.name: Bulging Charging Case / Swollen Lithium Cell
commonFaults.description: Lithium polymer pack swollen inside compact case, forcing plastic lid ajar.
diySteps: CRITICAL BATTERY HAZARD. Cease charging immediately.
Do not compress or attempt to close lid.
Bring to certified e-waste handler for safe neutralization.

categories.name: Fan or Cooler
categories.description: Ceiling fans, high-velocity table fans, pedestal fans, and evaporative desert coolers

safetyFlags.label: Motor winding burnt smell or smoking stator
Oscillation sheared power cable exposing live wire

repurposeIdeas.title: Workshop Fume & Solder Exhaust
repurposeIdeas.description: Mount high-RPM fan motor into a garage window duct to vent paint and solder vapors.

repurposeIdeas.title: Decorative Circular Garden Trellis
repurposeIdeas.description: Spray paint concentric metal fan safety grills and stake in garden for flowering vine climbers.

repurposeIdeas.title: DIY Wind Turbine Demo Model
repurposeIdeas.description: Reverse the motor hub using external magnets to create a demonstration wind energy generator.

reuseRoutes: Use in workshop, garage, or outdoor covered balcony where whisper-quiet operation is not required
Pass to security booth or local stall vendor
Sell to student hostel residents

repair: Cut circuit breaker or unplug cord completely before touching blades.
Discharge motor start capacitor safely across 100k ohm resistor.
Check bearing free-spinning resistance by hand spin.
Apply high-temperature synthetic bearing oil (SAE 20), avoid standard WD-40 on bronze bushings.
reuse: Unclip front metal grill and wash off dust pelt with soapy sponge.
Wipe aerodynamic blades to reduce motor drag.
Tighten blade hub screws to eliminate vibration rattles.
repurpose: Remove motor and wiring completely if making garden art.
Coat metal grills with rust-inhibiting zinc primer.
replace: Look for BLDC (Brushless DC) motor fans saving up to 65% electricity.
Check BEE 5-star label and remote control inverter ratings.
recycle: Copper motor stator windings have high scrap value; deliver to metal scrap yard.
Separate polypropylene fan blades and sheet metal grills.

commonFaults.label: Weak Run Capacitor (Fan Spins at Half Speed)
commonFaults.name: Weak Run Capacitor (Fan Spins at Half Speed)
commonFaults.description: Motor hums but rotates sluggishly; capacitor capacitance dropped below rated microfarads.
diySteps: Turn off mains wall switch and disconnect power.
Discharge old capacitor terminals by touching insulated screwdriver tip across leads.
Unscrew clamp, swap in new metallized polypropylene 2.25uF / 2.5uF 440V motor capacitor.
Restore power and test all 3 speed settings.

commonFaults.label: Dry / Seized Bushing Bearings (Squealing Noise)
commonFaults.name: Dry / Seized Bushing Bearings (Squealing Noise)
commonFaults.description: Dried-out porous bronze bushings causing friction squeal and thermal shutdown.
diySteps: Remove fan front grill, blade nut (reverse thread), and motor clam shell housing.
Clean old hardened gunk from steel shaft with mineral spirits.
Saturate felt oil reservoirs around sintered bronze bushings with 5-6 drops of non-detergent SAE 20 oil.
Spin rotor by hand until movement is buttery smooth.

commonFaults.label: Stripped Oscillation Gearbox (Clicks & Stalls)
commonFaults.name: Stripped Oscillation Gearbox (Clicks & Stalls)
commonFaults.description: Nylon reduction worm gear teeth stripped inside rear oscillation gearbox.
diySteps: Unscrew rear motor cap.
Remove 3 small screws holding clear gearbox cover.
Lift out stripped nylon gear cog and clean old grease.
Press in replacement gear, pack with white lithium grease, and fasten cover.

commonFaults.label: Submersible Water Pump Choked with Silt
commonFaults.name: Submersible Water Pump Choked with Silt
commonFaults.description: Cooler pump impeller choked by hard water scale and algae, preventing water circulation.
diySteps: Unplug cooler and drain bottom reservoir.
Twist off front magnetic impeller cap on submersible pump.
Soak cylindrical permanent magnet impeller in vinegar for 30 minutes to dissolve mineral scale.
Rinse, test pump in clean water bucket, and reinstall.

commonFaults.label: Stator Coil Burnt / Shorted Copper Winding
commonFaults.name: Stator Coil Burnt / Shorted Copper Winding
commonFaults.description: Thermal fuse bypassed or burned copper stator windings producing smoke.
diySteps: CRITICAL ELECTRICAL RISK. Motor core insulation has broken down.
Requires professional stator re-winding or replacement motor assembly.

commonFaults.label: Cable Sheath Severed by Oscillation Hinge
commonFaults.name: Cable Sheath Severed by Oscillation Hinge
commonFaults.description: Repetitive fan head swivel pinched cord against sharp metal hinge, exposing live 230V wires.
diySteps: Unplug immediately.
Cut damaged cable section out.
Re-route through protective rubber grommet with slack for full oscillation arc.
Reconnect internal terminal block and clamp tightly.

categories.name: Furniture
categories.description: Office chairs, dining tables, study desks, wooden cabinets, and bookshelves

safetyFlags.label: Chair or shelf joint collapsed under load
Sharp splintered edges or protruding nails

repurposeIdeas.title: Floating Wall Display Shelves
repurposeIdeas.description: Saw clean sections of undamaged desk tabletop or bookcase sides into stylish floating wall shelves.

repurposeIdeas.title: Rustic Garden Planter Bench
repurposeIdeas.description: Sand and weatherproof wooden dining chair frames to hold potted plants on patio or balcony.

repurposeIdeas.title: Cozy Raised Pet Bed
repurposeIdeas.description: Line a sturdy wooden drawer with soft cushion foam and fabric for an elevated cat/dog bed.

reuseRoutes: Pass to college students moving into unfurnished rental flats
Donate to community libraries, daycare centers, or NGOs
List on OLX / Freecycle for quick local porch pickup

repair: Identify whether wood is solid timber, MDF, or particleboard before choosing fasteners.
Scrape away old brittle dried glue from joint mortise and tenons.
Apply PVA cross-linking wood glue and clamp with bar clamps for minimum 12 hours.
Pre-drill pilot holes to prevent splitting near edges.
reuse: Thoroughly dust and clean with mild wood oil or mild detergent.
Tighten all loose bolts and corner bracket screws.
Stick felt floor protector pads under each leg.
repurpose: Unscrew all hardware and sort screws, hinges, and drawer runners.
Sand rough edges with 120-grit sandpaper.
Apply water-based varnish or chalk paint.
replace: Choose FSC-certified sustainably harvested timber.
Check weight capacity ratings and steel frame thickness.
Avoid low-grade unsealed particleboard prone to moisture swelling.
recycle: Remove metal drawer pulls and steel brackets for metal scrap.
Solid untreated timber can be chipped for garden mulch or biomass.

commonFaults.label: Wobbly Chair Legs / Loose Dowel Joints
commonFaults.name: Wobbly Chair Legs / Loose Dowel Joints
commonFaults.description: Dry mortise and tenon joint has worked loose over seasons of humidity changes.
diySteps: Gently tap loose joints apart with rubber mallet.
Scrape old dried yellow glue down to bare wood fibers.
Inject premium PVA aliphatic wood glue into sockets.
Reassemble joint and apply ratchet strap or bar clamp firmly for 24 hours.

commonFaults.label: Sinking Office Chair Gas Lift Cylinder
commonFaults.name: Sinking Office Chair Gas Lift Cylinder
commonFaults.description: Hydraulic nitrogen gas seal failed, slowly dropping chair height under body weight.
diySteps: Invert chair and tap wheel base off bottom shaft with rubber mallet.
Use pipe wrench around top of old cylinder to twist free from chair mechanism.
Drop standard Class 4 replacement pneumatic gas lift cylinder into base taper.
Sit down once to friction lock into place.

commonFaults.label: Broken Roller Drawer Runner / Ball Bearings
commonFaults.name: Broken Roller Drawer Runner / Ball Bearings
commonFaults.description: Drawer jams or derails due to bent steel track or missing ball bearings.
diySteps: Remove drawer and unscrew old metal runners from cabinet carcass.
Measure slide depth (e.g. 14, 16, or 18 inches).
Screw matching full-extension ball bearing telescopic slides onto pilot holes.
Re-insert drawer until latch clicks.

commonFaults.label: Torn Fabric / Peeling Faux Leather Cushion
commonFaults.name: Torn Fabric / Peeling Faux Leather Cushion
commonFaults.description: Upholstery worn through to cushion foam at seat edge.
diySteps: Unscrew seat bottom from chair frame.
Remove old staples with staple puller.
Stretch durable linen or vinyl upholstery fabric taut over foam.
Fire heavy-duty staples into underside plywood base every 2 cm.

commonFaults.label: Split Solid Timber Leg / Structural Crack
commonFaults.name: Split Solid Timber Leg / Structural Crack
commonFaults.description: Hardwood leg cracked along grain line from uneven tilting load.
diySteps: Pry split open slightly with thin blade.
Force wood glue deep into crack with syringe or thin card.
Clamp securely with 2 C-clamps; drill perpendicular hole and drive hidden fluted wooden dowel.
Wipe squeeze-out with damp cloth.

commonFaults.label: Peeling Edge Banding / Surface Veneer
commonFaults.name: Peeling Edge Banding / Surface Veneer
commonFaults.description: PVC or melamine edge tape peeling back, catching on clothing.
diySteps: Clean old dust under peeling strip.
Cover with baking paper and iron over edge with household clothes iron on medium heat to reactivate hot-melt glue.
Press down with wooden block until cooled, trim excess with utility knife.

categories.name: Bicycle
categories.description: Commuter cycles, road bicycles, mountain bikes, and geared hybrid bikes

safetyFlags.label: Brakes not gripping or cable snapped
Crack or buckling at welded frame headtube joint

repurposeIdeas.title: Indoor Stationary Fitness Spin Bike
repurposeIdeas.description: Mount onto an inexpensive magnetic resistance stand for indoor winter cardio workouts.

repurposeIdeas.title: Bicycle Handlebar & Seat Coat Rack
repurposeIdeas.description: Mount chrome drop handlebars and vintage leather saddle to wood as an eye-catching wall rack.

repurposeIdeas.title: Spoke Wheel Trellis or Giant Wall Clock
repurposeIdeas.description: Turn true steel rim and spokes into an outdoor garden climber or retro quartz clock face.

reuseRoutes: Donate to youth sports foundation or local cycling club
Pass to family member or daily station commuter
List on local sports exchange forums

repair: Invert bike or mount in repair stand to inspect moving drive train safely.
Check tire inflation pressure with Schrader/Presta pressure gauge.
Degrease chain and sprockets before applying dry PTFE or wet chain lube.
Torque axle nuts and handlebar stem bolts to safe manufacturer specifications.
reuse: Wash mud off frame, rims, and derailleur pivots.
Adjust seat post height so knee has slight 15-degree bend at bottom stroke.
Verify front and rear reflectors and bell are functional.
repurpose: Strip chain, cables, and brake calipers.
Clean metal tubing with degreaser and metal polish.
Securely anchor wall mounting hardware into masonry wall studs.
replace: Choose lightweight 6061 aluminium or chromoly steel frames.
Verify reliable Shimano or microSHIFT drivetrain componentry.
Pick mechanical or hydraulic disc brakes for wet weather stopping reliability.
recycle: Aluminium frame, steel spokes, and brass nipples have 100% scrap recycling efficiency.
Butyl rubber inner tubes can be recycled by local vulcanizing tire shops.

commonFaults.label: Flat Tire / Punctured Inner Tube
commonFaults.name: Flat Tire / Punctured Inner Tube
commonFaults.description: Thorn or glass sliver caused slow air leak in butyl tube.
diySteps: Unseat tire bead using 2 plastic tire levers.
Pull out tube and submerge in water bowl to pinpoint air bubbles.
Buff area with sandpaper, apply vulcanizing rubber cement, and press patch firmly for 3 minutes.
Check inside tire carcass with fingers for remaining thorns before re-installing.

commonFaults.label: Worn Rim Brake Pads / Poor Braking
commonFaults.name: Worn Rim Brake Pads / Poor Braking
commonFaults.description: Rubber brake pads worn down to steel wear line; squealing loudly against rim.
diySteps: Unscrew 5mm hex bolt securing pad to brake caliper arm.
Mount fresh all-weather rubber compound brake shoes.
Adjust alignment so pad strikes rim center squarely without touching tire rubber.
Toe-in pad front by 1 mm to prevent squealing.

commonFaults.label: Rusty / Sagging Drive Chain
commonFaults.name: Rusty / Sagging Drive Chain
commonFaults.description: Chain dried out and rusted from rain, causing stiff links and skipping sprockets.
diySteps: Scrub chain with brass wire brush and citrus degreaser to strip rust.
Check chain stretch with chain checker tool.
Apply single drop of synthetic bicycle chain lube to each roller.
Backpedal 20 rotations and wipe off excess surface oil.

commonFaults.label: Snapped Gear Derailleur Cable
commonFaults.name: Snapped Gear Derailleur Cable
commonFaults.description: Shifter cable frayed inside shifter pod, locking bike in smallest gear.
diySteps: Shift to highest gear setting and undo anchor bolt at rear derailleur.
Pull old cable through housing and thread new stainless steel slick cable.
Pull cable taut with pliers, tighten anchor bolt, and turn barrel adjuster to index gears.

commonFaults.label: Wobbly Wheel Rim / Rubbing Brake
commonFaults.name: Wobbly Wheel Rim / Rubbing Brake
commonFaults.description: Pothole impact loosened spoke tension, causing rim to wobble laterally.
diySteps: Mount bike upright and spin wheel against brake pad reference.
Where rim moves right, tighten left spoke nipple 1/4 turn and loosen right spoke 1/4 turn.
Continue fine tuning in small increments until lateral runout is under 1 mm.

commonFaults.label: Creaking Crank Bottom Bracket Bearings
commonFaults.name: Creaking Crank Bottom Bracket Bearings
commonFaults.description: Loud rhythmic click/creak every pedal stroke under hill climbing torque.
diySteps: Remove crank bolts and extract crank arms with crank puller tool.
Unscrew drive and non-drive bottom bracket cups (note reverse thread).
Clean frame bottom bracket shell threads, apply anti-seize grease, and install sealed cartridge unit.

categories.name: Bag or Footwear
categories.description: Travel backpacks, laptop rucksacks, leather boots, running sneakers, and duffel bags

safetyFlags.label: Broken sharp buckle edge or protruding wire eyelet

repurposeIdeas.title: Heavy-Duty Workshop Tool Apron
repurposeIdeas.description: Cut tough Cordura or canvas backpack panels into a multi-pocket tool and garden apron.

repurposeIdeas.title: Nylon Luggage Straps & Keyrings
repurposeIdeas.description: Salvage durable nylon webbing straps and quick-release buckles for motorcycle cargo tie-downs.

repurposeIdeas.title: EVA Foam Kneeling Gardening Pads
repurposeIdeas.description: Repurpose dense sneaker midsole foam or backpack lumbar cushioning into comfortable kneeling pads.

reuseRoutes: Donate lightly scuffed bags to underprivileged student book drives
Use as utility gym bag or trunk organizer in car
Pass along to community thrift stores or shelter clothing drives

repair: Clean dirt and oils from bond areas using rubbing alcohol.
Use curved heavy upholstery needles and bonded nylon thread (size #69) for fabric seams.
Apply contact cement (Barge or Shoe Goo) to both surfaces, let tack dry for 10 minutes before pressing.
Clamp bonded soles with rubber bands or heavy books for 24 hours.
reuse: Machine or hand wash in cold water with gentle detergent.
Treat leather shoes with conditioning cream and polish.
Replace worn interior insoles with fresh breathable memory foam insoles.
repurpose: Unpick stitching cleanly with seam ripper.
Trim raw fabric edges with pinking shears to stop fraying.
replace: Prioritize Goodyear welted footwear with re-soleable construction.
Look for backpacks made with 1000D Cordura and YKK size #10 zippers.
Check manufacturer repair warranty policies.
recycle: Drop shoes at Nike Grind or athletic footwear recycling bins at sports stores.
Remove brass grommets and metal zip sliders for scrap.

commonFaults.label: Separated Zipper Teeth / Broken Slider
commonFaults.name: Separated Zipper Teeth / Broken Slider
commonFaults.description: Zipper tracks split open behind the slider or pull tab broke off.
diySteps: Check zipper teeth are intact without missing plastic nubs.
If teeth don't interlock, slider gap has widened; gently squeeze slider cheeks with pliers.
If worn, cut top stop, slide on replacement matching slider (e.g. #5 or #8), and crimp new metal top stop.
Rub candle wax along track for smooth gliding.

commonFaults.label: Separated Outsole Flapping at Toe
commonFaults.name: Separated Outsole Flapping at Toe
commonFaults.description: Factory polyurethane adhesive degraded, causing toe or heel tread to flap open.
diySteps: Scrape old yellow glue and dust from both shoe upper and rubber sole.
Wipe clean with rubbing alcohol.
Apply thin coat of Shoe Goo or polyurethane contact adhesive to both surfaces.
Wait 8-10 minutes until tacky, press together firmly, and wrap tightly with strong elastic bands for 24 hours.
toolsRequired: Shoe Goo or Barge contact cement

commonFaults.label: Shoulder Strap Seam Pulled Out
commonFaults.name: Shoulder Strap Seam Pulled Out
commonFaults.description: Heavy laptop weight pulled bar-tack stitching out of top back seam.
diySteps: Tuck strap end 2 cm inside bag seam.
Thread heavy gauge bonded nylon thread through heavy curved hand needle.
Sew a reinforced 'box-X' stitch pattern through all fabric layers.
Knot securely and melt thread ends with lighter flame.

commonFaults.label: Worn Out Heel Rubber / Uneven Tread
commonFaults.name: Worn Out Heel Rubber / Uneven Tread
commonFaults.description: Outsole heel rubber worn down to hollow foam core, throwing off walking posture.
diySteps: Sand worn heel flat with 60-grit coarse sandpaper.
Coat replacement high-density rubber heel tap and shoe heel with contact adhesive.
Hammer together with shoe anvil or mallet, and trim perimeter flush with sharp hobby knife.

commonFaults.label: Cracked Side-Release Webbing Buckle
commonFaults.name: Cracked Side-Release Webbing Buckle
commonFaults.description: Plastic prong cracked after being slammed in car door.
diySteps: Snip cracked female or male buckle section off webbing loop.
Slide in a 'field repair' split-bar buckle without requiring any seam unpicking.
Pull webbing through tensioner to test hold.

commonFaults.label: Torn Ripstop Canvas or Lining Pocket
commonFaults.name: Torn Ripstop Canvas or Lining Pocket
commonFaults.description: Puncture hole or slit tear in backpack side or shoe lining.
diySteps: Round the corners of a self-adhesive nylon repair patch (e.g. Tenacious Tape) so edges don't lift.
Smooth torn canvas flat on table.
Press patch firmly over tear and rub with back of spoon to activate pressure-sensitive adhesive.
toolsRequired: Tenacious Tape or self-adhesive nylon patch

ka_blender_coupler.label: Stripped Drive Coupler Teeth
ka_blender_coupler.name: Stripped Drive Coupler Teeth
ka_blender_coupler.description: Rubber or nylon drive teeth rounded off from ice overload, causing motor to spin freely.
diySteps: Unplug appliance completely.
Hold motor shaft underneath with flathead screwdriver or cloth.
Unscrew coupler clockwise (reverse thread) and replace with identical replacement coupler.
Tighten securely and test with empty jar.

ka_kettle_switch.label: Auto-Shutoff Bimetal Switch Stuck
ka_kettle_switch.name: Auto-Shutoff Bimetal Switch Stuck
ka_kettle_switch.description: Steam bimetal strip fails to trigger switch off automatically when boiling.
diySteps: Unplug base and open kettle handle access screws.
Inspect steam tube channel for lime-scale deposits blocking vapor flow.
Gently clean contacts with isopropyl alcohol or replace standard T125 thermostat switch.
Reassemble handle and boil clean water to verify auto cut-off.

ka_motor_carbon_brushes.label: Worn Motor Carbon Brushes
ka_motor_carbon_brushes.name: Worn Motor Carbon Brushes
ka_motor_carbon_brushes.description: Motor sparks intermittently and runs sluggishly due to carbon brushes worn past minimum length.
diySteps: Unscrew motor base enclosure.
Unclip brass brush retainer springs.
Slide out worn carbon blocks and measure commutator ring surface.
Insert fresh brush pair and clip retainers back.

ka_heating_element.label: Blown Heating Element / Coil
ka_heating_element.name: Blown Heating Element / Coil
ka_heating_element.description: Appliance powers on indicator light but base produces zero heat.
diySteps: Check continuity across element terminals using multimeter resistance mode.
Detach heat-resistant push terminals and remove mounting flange nuts.
Fit matching OEM replacement heating ring or cartridge with new heatproof silicone gasket.

ka_burning_smell.label: Acrid Burning Odor / Coil Insulation Melting
ka_burning_smell.name: Acrid Burning Odor / Coil Insulation Melting
ka_burning_smell.description: Burnt varnish or melted wire sheath causing intense smoking and severe short circuit hazard.
diySteps: DO NOT USE DIY FIX. Requires professional coil rewinding or high-voltage insulation bench testing.

ka_mains_cord_frayed.label: Exposed Mains Copper Wire / Frayed Cable
ka_mains_cord_frayed.name: Exposed Mains Copper Wire / Frayed Cable
ka_mains_cord_frayed.description: Outer PVC jacket torn at strain-relief boot, revealing live mains conductors.
diySteps: Unplug immediately. Do not attempt tape-only repairs on 16A mains.
Open bottom cord clamp, trim off fatigued cable section.
Strip fresh insulation, crimp spade connectors, and anchor firmly into strain relief boot.

pl_battery_swollen.label: Swollen Puffy Lithium Battery (Display Lifting)
pl_battery_swollen.name: Swollen Puffy Lithium Battery (Display Lifting)
pl_battery_swollen.description: Gas buildup in lithium pouch causing acute fire/thermal runaway hazard.
diySteps: CRITICAL SAFETY HAZARD. Immediately stop charging and power off device.
Do not puncture, squeeze, or apply heat to the battery pouch.
Take immediately to certified technician equipped with fire-safe sand buckets.

pl_battery_degraded.label: Degraded Battery (Shuts down below 30%)
pl_battery_degraded.name: Degraded Battery (Shuts down below 30%)
pl_battery_degraded.description: Chemical capacity decayed under 75% health after years of charging cycles.
diySteps: Heat rear perimeter with warm gel pack to soften adhesive gasket.
Use suction cup and plastic guitar pick to gently lift back cover.
Unscrew battery bracket, disconnect flex cable, pull release adhesive tabs.
Install fresh OEM battery cell and reapply adhesive perimeter.

pl_cracked_screen.label: Cracked Front Glass / Touch Display
pl_cracked_screen.name: Cracked Front Glass / Touch Display
pl_cracked_screen.description: Spiderweb glass fracture from drop impact; touch digitizer or AMOLED panel damaged.
diySteps: Apply clear packing tape over splintered glass to avoid finger cuts.
Disconnect battery connector first before disconnecting display ribbon.
Transfer ambient light sensor and speaker mesh to new display assembly.
Connect new display, test all touch points and brightness before final adhesive clamping.

pl_charging_port_clogged.label: Loose / Lint-Clogged USB-C Port
pl_charging_port_clogged.name: Loose / Lint-Clogged USB-C Port
pl_charging_port_clogged.description: Cable falls out easily and fast charging drops due to packed pocket lint in port recess.
diySteps: Turn off device and illuminate port with bright flashlight.
Use non-conductive wooden toothpick or plastic probe to gently extract compressed lint.
Blow dry compressed air burst to clear dislodged fibers.
Insert cable firmly until tactile click confirms full engagement.

pl_cooling_fan_buzzing.label: Dust-Choked Fan / Thermal Throttling
pl_cooling_fan_buzzing.name: Dust-Choked Fan / Thermal Throttling
pl_cooling_fan_buzzing.description: Laptop runs burning hot and fan buzzes loudly due to dust pelt blocking heatsink fins.
diySteps: Remove bottom chassis screws and pry cover.
Hold fan blades stationary with finger so bearings do not overspin.
Brush dust felt from copper heatsink fins and vacuum gently.
Apply drop of fresh thermal paste on CPU/GPU if heat pipe was removed.

pl_keyboard_keys_stuck.label: Sticky / Non-Registering Keyboard Keys
pl_keyboard_keys_stuck.name: Sticky / Non-Registering Keyboard Keys
pl_keyboard_keys_stuck.description: Beverage spill residue or debris underneath scissor switch hinge.
diySteps: Gently pop off offending keycap using thin pry tool.
Clean scissor mechanism and rubber dome with 99% isopropyl alcohol swab.
Allow 15 minutes to dry fully, snap keycap back down until it clicks.

cc_cable_frayed_neck.label: Outer Sheath Frayed at Connector Boot
cc_cable_frayed_neck.name: Outer Sheath Frayed at Connector Boot
cc_cable_frayed_neck.description: Strain relief collar split open; braided shielding or internal conductors visible.
diySteps: Check internal copper strands are still intact without shorting.
Slide marine-grade adhesive-lined polyolefin heat-shrink tubing over connector head.
Shrink with heat gun or hair dryer until adhesive oozes slightly, forming stiff reinforced boot.
Add silicone cable spring collar for extra flex resistance.

cc_intermittent_connection.label: Intermittent Charging (Wire Broken Inside Neck)
cc_intermittent_connection.name: Intermittent Charging (Wire Broken Inside Neck)
cc_intermittent_connection.description: Charges only when bent at a specific angle due to fatigue fracture in copper hair wires.
diySteps: Cut cable 2 cm back from damaged molded plug.
Strip outer jacket to expose internal conductor cores.
Solder leads onto a DIY solderable metal USB-C / Lightning plug replacement head.
Snap outer metal shielding shell and crimp strain relief.

cc_bent_pin.label: Bent Connector Plug / Housing
cc_bent_pin.name: Bent Connector Plug / Housing
cc_bent_pin.description: Metal shell squished or bent from being stepped on, preventing port insertion.
diySteps: Carefully inspect interior tongue with magnifying loupe.
Use flat precision watchmaker screwdriver to gently reform outer rectangular metal shield.
Verify pins are not shorted before plugging into low-value device.

cc_corroded_contacts.label: Tarnished / Blackened Gold Pins
cc_corroded_contacts.name: Tarnished / Blackened Gold Pins
cc_corroded_contacts.description: Blackened oxide coating on power pins causing slow or failed charging handshake.
diySteps: Dip stiff bristle interdental brush into 99% isopropyl alcohol.
Scrub contact pins back and forth vigorously to remove carbonization.
Dry with microfiber cloth and apply thin coat of DeoxIT contact cleaner.

cc_adapter_overheating.label: Wall Adapter Burning Smell / Melting Shell
cc_adapter_overheating.name: Wall Adapter Burning Smell / Melting Shell
cc_adapter_overheating.description: Blown primary switching MOSFET or shorted transformer winding generating smoke.
diySteps: CRITICAL FIRE HAZARD. Immediately unplug from mains.
Ultrasonically welded power bricks cannot be safely opened or resealed at home.
Recycle immediately and replace with compliant charger.

ad_earcup_padding_peeling.label: Flaking Leatherette Ear Cushions
ad_earcup_padding_peeling.name: Flaking Leatherette Ear Cushions
ad_earcup_padding_peeling.description: Polyurethane leather flakes off in black specks onto ears, though audio drivers remain pristine.
diySteps: Gently rotate or unclip old cushion plastic retaining rings.
Clean old adhesive residue with isopropyl swab.
Stretch replacement breathable velour or cooling gel ear pads over headphone rim and click firmly into place.

ad_headband_snapped.label: Snapped Plastic Headband Arch
ad_headband_snapped.name: Snapped Plastic Headband Arch
ad_headband_snapped.description: Tension arch cracked at stress point, preventing headphones from clamping to head.
diySteps: Rough up plastic edges with 220-grit sandpaper.
Splint crack with thin flexible spring steel strip or zip-tie reinforcement.
Bond with two-part epoxy or wrap tightly with self-amalgamating silicone tape.

ad_one_side_silent.label: One Channel Silent (Frayed Jack Wire)
ad_one_side_silent.name: One Channel Silent (Frayed Jack Wire)
ad_one_side_silent.description: Sound cuts out in left or right ear unless 3.5mm plug is wiggled.
diySteps: Snip off factory molded 3.5mm plug 3 cm from bend.
Burn enamel insulation off copper hairs with lighter flame, then tin with solder flux.
Solder Left (tip), Right (ring), and Ground (sleeve) onto metal replacement 3.5mm TRS jack.

ad_battery_draining_fast.label: Battery Lasts Under 30 Minutes
ad_battery_draining_fast.name: Battery Lasts Under 30 Minutes
ad_battery_draining_fast.description: Internal 3.7V lithium pouch holds fraction of original charge.
diySteps: Unclip ear cup cover and unscrew internal acoustic baffle.
De-solder red (+) and black (-) leads from old lithium cell.
Fit identical dimension 3.7V lipo cell with protection circuit board.
Re-solder leads, secure with double-sided foam tape, and reassemble.

ad_swollen_earbud_case.label: Bulging Charging Case / Swollen Lithium Cell
ad_swollen_earbud_case.name: Bulging Charging Case / Swollen Lithium Cell
ad_swollen_earbud_case.description: Lithium polymer pack swollen inside compact case, forcing plastic lid ajar.
diySteps: CRITICAL BATTERY HAZARD. Cease charging immediately.
Do not compress or attempt to close lid.
Bring to certified e-waste handler for safe neutralization.

fc_capacitor_weak.label: Weak Run Capacitor (Fan Spins at Half Speed)
fc_capacitor_weak.name: Weak Run Capacitor (Fan Spins at Half Speed)
fc_capacitor_weak.description: Motor hums but rotates sluggishly; capacitor capacitance dropped below rated microfarads.
diySteps: Turn off mains wall switch and disconnect power.
Discharge old capacitor terminals by touching insulated screwdriver tip across leads.
Unscrew clamp, swap in new metallized polypropylene 2.25uF / 2.5uF 440V motor capacitor.
Restore power and test all 3 speed settings.

fc_bearing_jammed.label: Dry / Seized Bushing Bearings (Squealing Noise)
fc_bearing_jammed.name: Dry / Seized Bushing Bearings (Squealing Noise)
fc_bearing_jammed.description: Dried-out porous bronze bushings causing friction squeal and thermal shutdown.
diySteps: Remove fan front grill, blade nut (reverse thread), and motor clam shell housing.
Clean old hardened gunk from steel shaft with mineral spirits.
Saturate felt oil reservoirs around sintered bronze bushings with 5-6 drops of non-detergent SAE 20 oil.
Spin rotor by hand until movement is buttery smooth.

fc_oscillation_gear_stripped.label: Stripped Oscillation Gearbox (Clicks & Stalls)
fc_oscillation_gear_stripped.name: Stripped Oscillation Gearbox (Clicks & Stalls)
fc_oscillation_gear_stripped.description: Nylon reduction worm gear teeth stripped inside rear oscillation gearbox.
diySteps: Unscrew rear motor cap.
Remove 3 small screws holding clear gearbox cover.
Lift out stripped nylon gear cog and clean old grease.
Press in replacement gear, pack with white lithium grease, and fasten cover.

fc_pump_choked.label: Submersible Water Pump Choked with Silt
fc_pump_choked.name: Submersible Water Pump Choked with Silt
fc_pump_choked.description: Cooler pump impeller choked by hard water scale and algae, preventing water circulation.
diySteps: Unplug cooler and drain bottom reservoir.
Twist off front magnetic impeller cap on submersible pump.
Soak cylindrical permanent magnet impeller in vinegar for 30 minutes to dissolve mineral scale.
Rinse, test pump in clean water bucket, and reinstall.

fc_motor_burning_odor.label: Stator Coil Burnt / Shorted Copper Winding
fc_motor_burning_odor.name: Stator Coil Burnt / Shorted Copper Winding
fc_motor_burning_odor.description: Thermal fuse bypassed or burned copper stator windings producing smoke.
diySteps: CRITICAL ELECTRICAL RISK. Motor core insulation has broken down.
Requires professional stator re-winding or replacement motor assembly.

fc_exposed_cut_cord.label: Cable Sheath Severed by Oscillation Hinge
fc_exposed_cut_cord.name: Cable Sheath Severed by Oscillation Hinge
fc_exposed_cut_cord.description: Repetitive fan head swivel pinched cord against sharp metal hinge, exposing live 230V wires.
diySteps: Unplug immediately.
Cut damaged cable section out.
Re-route through protective rubber grommet with slack for full oscillation arc.
Reconnect internal terminal block and clamp tightly.

fn_loose_joints_wobble.label: Wobbly Chair Legs / Loose Dowel Joints
fn_loose_joints_wobble.name: Wobbly Chair Legs / Loose Dowel Joints
fn_loose_joints_wobble.description: Dry mortise and tenon joint has worked loose over seasons of humidity changes.
diySteps: Gently tap loose joints apart with rubber mallet.
Scrape old dried yellow glue down to bare wood fibers.
Inject premium PVA aliphatic wood glue into sockets.
Reassemble joint and apply ratchet strap or bar clamp firmly for 24 hours.

fn_gas_lift_cylinder_sinking.label: Sinking Office Chair Gas Lift Cylinder
fn_gas_lift_cylinder_sinking.name: Sinking Office Chair Gas Lift Cylinder
fn_gas_lift_cylinder_sinking.description: Hydraulic nitrogen gas seal failed, slowly dropping chair height under body weight.
diySteps: Invert chair and tap wheel base off bottom shaft with rubber mallet.
Use pipe wrench around top of old cylinder to twist free from chair mechanism.
Drop standard Class 4 replacement pneumatic gas lift cylinder into base taper.
Sit down once to friction lock into place.

fn_broken_drawer_slide.label: Broken Roller Drawer Runner / Ball Bearings
fn_broken_drawer_slide.name: Broken Roller Drawer Runner / Ball Bearings
fn_broken_drawer_slide.description: Drawer jams or derails due to bent steel track or missing ball bearings.
diySteps: Remove drawer and unscrew old metal runners from cabinet carcass.
Measure slide depth (e.g. 14, 16, or 18 inches).
Screw matching full-extension ball bearing telescopic slides onto pilot holes.
Re-insert drawer until latch clicks.

fn_upholstery_tear.label: Torn Fabric / Peeling Faux Leather Cushion
fn_upholstery_tear.name: Torn Fabric / Peeling Faux Leather Cushion
fn_upholstery_tear.description: Upholstery worn through to cushion foam at seat edge.
diySteps: Unscrew seat bottom from chair frame.
Remove old staples with staple puller.
Stretch durable linen or vinyl upholstery fabric taut over foam.
Fire heavy-duty staples into underside plywood base every 2 cm.

fn_snapped_chair_leg.label: Split Solid Timber Leg / Structural Crack
fn_snapped_chair_leg.name: Split Solid Timber Leg / Structural Crack
fn_snapped_chair_leg.description: Hardwood leg cracked along grain line from uneven tilting load.
diySteps: Pry split open slightly with thin blade.
Force wood glue deep into crack with syringe or thin card.
Clamp securely with 2 C-clamps; drill perpendicular hole and drive hidden fluted wooden dowel.
Wipe squeeze-out with damp cloth.

fn_cracked_laminate.label: Peeling Edge Banding / Surface Veneer
fn_cracked_laminate.name: Peeling Edge Banding / Surface Veneer
fn_cracked_laminate.description: PVC or melamine edge tape peeling back, catching on clothing.
diySteps: Clean old dust under peeling strip.
Cover with baking paper and iron over edge with household clothes iron on medium heat to reactivate hot-melt glue.
Press down with wooden block until cooled, trim excess with utility knife.

by_punctured_tube.label: Flat Tire / Punctured Inner Tube
by_punctured_tube.name: Flat Tire / Punctured Inner Tube
by_punctured_tube.description: Thorn or glass sliver caused slow air leak in butyl tube.
diySteps: Unseat tire bead using 2 plastic tire levers.
Pull out tube and submerge in water bowl to pinpoint air bubbles.
Buff area with sandpaper, apply vulcanizing rubber cement, and press patch firmly for 3 minutes.
Check inside tire carcass with fingers for remaining thorns before re-installing.

by_brake_pads_worn.label: Worn Rim Brake Pads / Poor Braking
by_brake_pads_worn.name: Worn Rim Brake Pads / Poor Braking
by_brake_pads_worn.description: Rubber brake pads worn down to steel wear line; squealing loudly against rim.
diySteps: Unscrew 5mm hex bolt securing pad to brake caliper arm.
Mount fresh all-weather rubber compound brake shoes.
Adjust alignment so pad strikes rim center squarely without touching tire rubber.
Toe-in pad front by 1 mm to prevent squealing.

by_chain_rusty_slack.label: Rusty / Sagging Drive Chain
by_chain_rusty_slack.name: Rusty / Sagging Drive Chain
by_chain_rusty_slack.description: Chain dried out and rusted from rain, causing stiff links and skipping sprockets.
diySteps: Scrub chain with brass wire brush and citrus degreaser to strip rust.
Check chain stretch with chain checker tool.
Apply single drop of synthetic bicycle chain lube to each roller.
Backpedal 20 rotations and wipe off excess surface oil.

by_shifter_cable_snapped.label: Snapped Gear Derailleur Cable
by_shifter_cable_snapped.name: Snapped Gear Derailleur Cable
by_shifter_cable_snapped.description: Shifter cable frayed inside shifter pod, locking bike in smallest gear.
diySteps: Shift to highest gear setting and undo anchor bolt at rear derailleur.
Pull old cable through housing and thread new stainless steel slick cable.
Pull cable taut with pliers, tighten anchor bolt, and turn barrel adjuster to index gears.

by_wheel_out_of_true.label: Wobbly Wheel Rim / Rubbing Brake
by_wheel_out_of_true.name: Wobbly Wheel Rim / Rubbing Brake
by_wheel_out_of_true.description: Pothole impact loosened spoke tension, causing rim to wobble laterally.
diySteps: Mount bike upright and spin wheel against brake pad reference.
Where rim moves right, tighten left spoke nipple 1/4 turn and loosen right spoke 1/4 turn.
Continue fine tuning in small increments until lateral runout is under 1 mm.

by_bottom_bracket_creak.name: Creaking Crank Bottom Bracket Bearings
by_bottom_bracket_creak.description: Loud rhythmic click/creak every pedal stroke under hill climbing torque.
diySteps: Remove crank bolts and extract crank arms with crank puller tool.
Unscrew drive and non-drive bottom bracket cups (note reverse thread).
Clean frame bottom bracket shell threads, apply anti-seize grease, and install sealed cartridge unit.

bf_zipper_slider_separated.name: Separated Zipper Teeth / Broken Slider
bf_zipper_slider_separated.description: Zipper tracks split open behind the slider or pull tab broke off.

If teeth don't interlock, slider gap has widened; gently squeeze slider cheeks with pliers.
If worn, cut top stop, slide on replacement matching slider (e.g. #5 or #8), and crimp new metal top stop.
Rub candle wax along track for smooth gliding.

Wait 8-10 minutes until tacky, press together firmly, and wrap tightly with strong elastic bands for 24 hours.

bf_strap_stitching_torn.name: Shoulder Strap Seam Pulled Out
bf_strap_stitching_torn.description: Heavy laptop weight pulled bar-tack stitching out of top back seam.
diySteps: Tuck strap end 2 cm inside bag seam.
Thread heavy gauge bonded nylon thread through heavy curved hand needle.
Sew a reinforced 'box-X' stitch pattern through all fabric layers.
Knot securely and melt thread ends with lighter flame.

bf_worn_heel_tap.label: Worn Out Heel Rubber / Uneven Tread
bf_worn_heel_tap.name: Worn Out Heel Rubber / Uneven Tread
bf_worn_heel_tap.description: Outsole heel rubber worn down to hollow foam core, throwing off walking posture.
diySteps: Sand worn heel flat with 60-grit coarse sandpaper.
Coat replacement high-density rubber heel tap and shoe heel with contact adhesive.
Hammer together with shoe anvil or mallet, and trim perimeter flush with sharp hobby knife.

bf_snapped_plastic_buckle.label: Cracked Side-Release Webbing Buckle
bf_snapped_plastic_buckle.name: Cracked Side-Release Webbing Buckle
bf_snapped_plastic_buckle.description: Plastic prong cracked after being slammed in car door.
diySteps: Snip cracked female or male buckle section off webbing loop.
Slide in a 'field repair' split-bar buckle without requiring any seam unpicking.
Pull webbing through tensioner to test hold.

bf_canvas_tear.label: Torn Ripstop Canvas or Lining Pocket
bf_canvas_tear.name: Torn Ripstop Canvas or Lining Pocket
bf_canvas_tear.description: Puncture hole or slit tear in backpack side or shoe lining.
diySteps: Round the corners of a self-adhesive nylon repair patch (e.g. Tenacious Tape) so edges don't lift.
Smooth torn canvas flat on table.
Press patch firmly over tear and rub with back of spoon to activate pressure-sensitive adhesive.

lever_wont_latch.label: Lever won't latch down
lever_wont_latch.name: Lever won't latch down
lever_wont_latch.description: Toaster carriage won't lock down due to crumb accumulation or dirty electromagnet.
diySteps: Unplug toaster
Empty crumb tray
Gently clean latch hook with soft brush

sparks_inside.label: Sparks inside microwave casing
sparks_inside.name: Sparks inside microwave casing
sparks_inside.safetyWarning: Arcing sparks usually caused by food splatter burning through mica waveguide cover.

swollen_battery.label: Swollen lithium battery
swollen_battery.name: Swollen lithium battery
